title: LOOKUP vs VLOOKUP: why the old one still shows up
meta_desc: The bare LOOKUP function vs VLOOKUP: vector form, always-approximate matching, the last-non-blank trick, and when either is the wrong choice today.
intro: Bare LOOKUP predates VLOOKUP and survives for two reasons: its vector form is pleasantly direct (lookup range and result range as separate arguments — like a primitive XLOOKUP), and its always-approximate matching powers classic tricks like finding the last non-blank cell. As a general lookup, though, it's a trap.

cols: ALWAYS approximate — assumes sorted data, no exact option
Approximate by default, exact with FALSE
No — index into one table, rightward only
Universal (both verified in every version we test)

when.use_when: Two situations only: genuinely sorted threshold data where you'd use approximate matching anyway, and the last-non-blank/last-match idioms built on its scan-to-the-end behavior.
Ordinary exact lookups in older-version-compatible sheets (always passing FALSE). On modern versions, XLOOKUP supersedes both — it has LOOKUP's separate-ranges design plus an exact-match default.

compat_note: Both execute identically in every LibreOffice build and in the Google Sheets run we execute (Excel per Microsoft's docs — we do not run Excel) — LOOKUP's dangers are semantic (silent approximate matching), not compatibility. XLOOKUP, the modern replacement for both, needs Excel 2021+/365, current Sheets, or LibreOffice 24.8+ per our executed results.
